Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals briefly stated are that on 14.01.2017, the deceased Mareppa and the injured Balappa were proceeding on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-33/U-4286 from Krishnapur to Mandagalli.
Mareppa was riding the motorcycle and Balappa was the pillion rider.

When they reached near the Mandagalli camp situated on the Shahapur to Shorapur Main road, at that time, a Mahindra Max Pick Up bearing registration No.KA-35/A-3752 which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, came from opposite side and dashed against the motorcycle ridden by deceased Mareppa.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, both fell down and sustained grievous injuries, and Mareppa succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
4. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased Mareppa along with interest.

It was pleaded that the injured Balappa spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related NC:
Laxmi And Ors vs Mohammed Ali And Anr on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133989133/
5 2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR costs.

sentences.text: It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
5. In MVC.No.774/2017, upon service of notice, respondent Nos.1, 2 and 4 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The respondent No.3, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.
In MVC.No.753/2017, upon service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

6. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimant in MVC.No.774/2017 is entitled to a compensation of Rs.9,03,200/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., and claimants in MVC.No.753/2017 are NC:
2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR entitled to a compensation of Rs.23,45,600/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeals have been filed.

The learned counsel appearing for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the claimant asserts that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by working as Mason and Rs.2,00,000/- per annum as agriculturist.
However, the Tribunal has erred in taking the income as merely as Rs.10,250/- per month.
b) Secondly, the claimant has examined the doctor as PW-2.
The Tribunal undervalued the claimant's whole-body disability at 17%, contradicting the evidence of the doctor that the claimant suffered 50% disability to whole body.
c) Thirdly, due to the accident, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
He was treated as inpatient for NC: 2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR a period of 62 days.
Even after discharge from the hospital, he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment.
Considering the same, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
d) Lastly, the evidence of the doctor suggests that the claimant requires Rs.40,000/- for removal of implants.
The Tribunal has granted only Rs.15,000/- towards 'Future Medical Expenses'.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeal.

8. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2-Sriram General Insurance Company has raised the following counter-contentions:

a) Firstly, the assertion of claimant that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month as mason and Rs.2,00,000/-
annually as agriculturist, remains unsubstantiated due to lack of documentary evidence.
In the absence of proof of - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR income, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the claimant notionally.

b) Secondly, even though the doctor deposed that the claimant suffered 50% disability to the whole body, the Tribunal has taken 1/3rd of the disability assessed by the doctor and has considered the whole body disability as 17%, which is just and reasonable.

c) Thirdly, considering the injuries sustained by the claimant and considering the age and avocation of the claimant, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable and it does not warrant interference.
d) Lastly, the doctor has deposed that the claimant requires Rs.40,000/- for removal of the implant.

Considering the injuries suffered by the claimant, the disability certificate, and the medical records,
the Tribunal has rightly granted Rs.15,000/- towards 'Future medical expenses'.

With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to dismiss the appeal.
9. Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4 - ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company has submitted that the Tribunal has not fastened any liability on it.

10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
11.
It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 14.01.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

12. The claimant claims that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month as mason and Rs.2,00,000/-
per annum as agriculturist.
But he has not produced any documents to substantiate his claim.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, notional income has to be assessed.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed monthly income of the claimant as Rs.10,250/- per month.

As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained below injuries:
i) Compound comminuted fracture of shaft of right femur with bone loss.
ii) Compound comminuted fracture of upper 3rd right tibia and other grievous injuries over the vital parts of the body.

14. Taking into consideration the deposition of the doctor that the claimant has pain and swelling in the right thigh and leg, is unable to fold his right knee, cannot walk without support, and is unable to squat or sit cross-legged and further considering that the surgery, one inch shortening of the right lower limb along with injuries mentioned in the wound certificate, we are of the opinion that the whole body disability has to be assessed at 25%.
The claimant is aged about 38 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '15'.
Thus, the claimant is entitled for compensation of - 13 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR Rs.4,61,250/- (Rs.10,250*12*15*25%) on account of 'loss of future income'.
15. Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injuries and also undergone surgery.
The claimant was hospitalized as an inpatient for more than 62 days in the hospital and subsequently received further treatment.

Considering the prolonged pain during treatment as well as the permanent disability certified by the doctor, we are inclined to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'pain and sufferings' from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.60,000/- and under the head of 'loss of amenities' from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.30,000/-.
16. Although the evidence of the doctor suggests that the claimant requires approximately Rs.40,000/- for removal of implants, the claimant has not provided any estimate for future surgery.

Considering the nature of the injuries and the evidence of the doctor, we are inclined to - 14 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'future medical expenses' from Rs.15,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
17. Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.

18. Thus, the claimant is entitled to the following compensation:

The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the claimants assert that the deceased was aged about 27 years at the time of the accident and had a monthly income of Rs.15,000/- and Rs.150/- per day as Bhatta by working as driver under PW.2.
Therefore, the assessment of monthly income of the deceased at Rs.10,250/- by the Tribunal is unjustified and erroneous.

b) Secondly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157], in cases, where the deceased was self- Laxmi And Ors vs Mohammed Ali And Anr on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133989133/
9 employed or received a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income towards 'future prospects' is - 16 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR warranted when the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
The said principle is rightly applied to the present case.

c) Thirdly, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ 2782], each of the claimants is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of love and affection and consortium'.
d) Lastly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate and on the lower side.

sentences.text: With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeal.

20. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter- contentions:
a) Firstly, although the claimants claim that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/-
per month, they have failed to substantiate their claim with supporting - 17 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR documents.
Consequently, the Tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased notionally.

b) Secondly, since the claimants have not established the income of the deceased, they are not entitled for compensation towards 'future prospects'.
c) Thirdly, on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence and considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to dismiss the appeal.

21. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
22.
It is not in dispute that Mareppa died in the road traffic accident occurred on 14.01.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

23. The claimants claim that deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month and Bhatta of Rs.150/- as a driver Laxmi And Ors vs Mohammed Ali And Anr on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133989133/

Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional income of the deceased as Rs.10,250/-pm.,
Accordingly, loss of dependency assessed by Tribunal is just and reasonable.

24. Considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal on other heads is just and reasonable and it does not call for interference in the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
25. In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal in MFA No.202530/2022 is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.11,35,784/-.

- 19 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR d) The Respondent No.2 - Sriram General Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
However, the compensation awarded under the head of 'future medical expenses' shall not carry any interest.
e) The deposit and release of amount shall be made in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
f) The appeal filed by the claimants in MFA.No.202542/2022 is dismissed confirming the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.753/2017.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Mareppa was riding the motorcycle and Balappa was the pillion rider.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, both fell down and sustained grievous injuries, and Mareppa succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
4. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased Mareppa along with interest.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimant in MVC.No.774/2017 is entitled to a compensation of Rs.9,03,200/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., and claimants in MVC.No.753/2017 are NC:
2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR entitled to a compensation of Rs.23,45,600/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
However, the Tribunal has erred in taking the income as merely as Rs.10,250/- per month.
The Tribunal undervalued the claimant's whole-body disability at 17%, contradicting the evidence of the doctor that the claimant suffered 50% disability to whole body.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed monthly income of the claimant as Rs.10,250/- per month.
17. Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 14.01.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
But he has not produced any documents to substantiate his claim.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, notional income has to be assessed.
The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the claimants assert that the deceased was aged about 27 years at the time of the accident and had a monthly income of Rs.15,000/- and Rs.150/- per day as Bhatta by working as driver under PW.2.
Therefore, the assessment of monthly income of the deceased at Rs.10,250/- by the Tribunal is unjustified and erroneous.
Consequently, the Tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased notionally.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
b) Secondly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157], in cases, where the deceased was self- Laxmi And Ors vs Mohammed Ali And Anr on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133989133/
9 employed or received a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income towards 'future prospects' is - 16 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR warranted when the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
The said principle is rightly applied to the present case.
c) Thirdly, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ 2782], each of the claimants is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of love and affection and consortium'.
d) Lastly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate and on the lower side.
opennyai_summary.decision:
24. Considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal on other heads is just and reasonable and it does not call for interference in the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
25. In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal in MFA No.202530/2022 is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.11,35,784/-.
- 19 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7506-DB HC-KAR d) The Respondent No.2 - Sriram General Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
However, the compensation awarded under the head of 'future medical expenses' shall not carry any interest.
e) The deposit and release of amount shall be made in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
f) The appeal filed by the claimants in MFA.No.202542/2022 is dismissed confirming the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.753/2017.
